Medium: ONLY matte hand-cut paper in thin broad flat layers. Subtle paper grain, crisp scissor-cut silhouettes, small flat-paper inlays, restrained layered shadows. No thick rolled quilling, no photographic flesh/soil, no clay toys, leather, glossy plastic or shiny 3D CGI.
Warm ivory paper studio background for isolated subjects, muted earth/olive/brown/indigo palette; gentle consistent diffuse light.
No captions, letters, watermarks, labels, ornamental border, fake sacred symbols, gold crowns, carnival feather costumes, jewelry or additional figures. Exact quantities and identity consistency are critical. Original fictional adaptation; do not claim ethnic biometric authenticity or clone real photographed people.
Subject: ONE large living crocodilian called caimán in myth365; species is NOT established by the story. Anatomical inspiration only: elongated fairly narrow tapered snout, eyes/nasal openings on top, interlocking natural teeth, low heavy body, FOUR short sprawling legs, longitudinal dorsal scute rows and ONE long laterally flattened ridged tail. Matte muted grey-olive/tan PAPER, not uniformly emerald green dinosaur scales. No horns, humanoid eyes, costume, blood, injury or medical anatomy.
Composition: FOUR separated study panels vertically arranged with adequate margins. Panel1: entire same animal in left-facing side/three-quarter shore stance, complete body, all limbs properly placed and full tail visible. Panel2: same animal swimming, eyes/snouthigh and back/tail at surface in a small flat-paper blue-grey water swatch; tail remains crocodilian. Panel3: same animal in complete side view with jaws naturally open; plausible jaw hinge, natural teeth, no person or weapon in its mouth. Panel4: isolated ONE large smooth pale oval dream egg next to a small simple flat-paper ground swatch, without animal/person overlay. Egg size is narrative/editorial and provisional, not a scientific zoological claim.
Same crocodilian morphology in all THREE animal views; FOURTH panel is egg only. ZERO humans, ZERO arrows, no anatomy of stomach/interior; that narrative space is a separate future L11.
